headline: Earnings rebound as medical costs ease; guidance raised
summary_short: UnitedHealth's Q2 2026 revenue was $112.0B (+0.4% y/y) as the medical care ratio improved to 86.7% from 89.4% a year ago, lifting operating earnings to $8.0B (+55.2% y/y) and diluted EPS to $6.04 (+61.5% y/y, adjusted $6.38); the company raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $19.50-$20.00.
summary_long: Revenue rose modestly to $112.0B (+0.4% y/y, +0.3% q/q) as UnitedHealthcare revenue held roughly flat at $86.0B and Optum revenue fell to $65.7B on Optum Health value-based-care attrition. The medical care ratio improved to 86.7% from 89.4% a year ago on benefit design, pricing discipline, and $860M of net favorable prior-period development, lifting earnings from operations to $8.0B (+55.2% y/y) though down 11.1% q/q from Q1's unusually strong print. Diluted EPS was $6.04 (+61.5% y/y, adjusted $6.38). Cash and short-term investments rose to $31.5B from $28.1B at year-end as Q2 operating cash flow was $11.1B, 1.9x net income. UnitedHealth raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $19.50-$20.00 from prior guidance of >$17.75, citing year-to-date performance and an improved outlook.

drivers.explanation: CEO Stephen Hemsley cited continuing progress simplifying operations and improving affordability; the company reported Q2 results and raised full-year 2026 guidance on year-to-date performance.

UnitedHealthcare revenue was roughly flat at $86.0B (48.5M served, down 525,000 sequentially) while Optum revenue fell to $65.7B, driven by Optum Health's ~700,000 fewer value-based-care patients served.
Not explained in the release; this GAAP 'Cost of products sold' line item is not itself discussed in the release's narrative, which addresses medical costs and operating costs separately.

Earnings from operations rose y/y as the medical care ratio fell to 86.7% from 89.4% on benefit design, pricing discipline, member mix, and $860M of net favorable prior-period development; the sequential decline from Q1's $9.0B is not itemized in the release.
Tracks the earnings-from-operations improvement; interest expense fell slightly to $962M from $1,027M y/y. The release does not separately narrate below-the-line items.
Net income growth is arithmetically consistent with the pretax income increase, partly offset by a higher tax provision ($1,298M vs $510M y/y); the release does not itemize the tax-rate change.
Diluted EPS growth (+61.5% y/y) is arithmetically consistent with net income growth (+61.0% y/y) plus a small reduction in diluted share count from ongoing buybacks (906M vs 910M).
Basic EPS growth tracks net income growth on a slightly smaller basic share count than diluted; not separately narrated in the release.

Cash and cash equivalents were roughly flat y/y; the cash flow statement shows $20.0B of six-month operating cash flow largely offset by $1.6B of buybacks, $4.1B of dividends, and $4.8B of net debt paydown.
Long-term debt declined as the company continues paying down debt toward its targeted ~40% debt-to-capital ratio (41.2% at Q2 2026 vs 44.1% a year ago).
Not explained in the release beyond the overall debt-to-capital reduction; no specific maturity or refinancing detail is given for the current-portion decline.
Equity growth is arithmetically consistent with retained net earnings, partly offset by $1.6B of buybacks and $4.1B of dividends paid over the six months.
The modest share-count decline reflects ongoing buybacks; the company repurchased $4.0B of stock through mid-July 2026 and is on track for at least $5.0B for the full year.
